title: Unified tool-adapter proposal: reconcile OpenAI-style tools with legacy functions and streaming semantics
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: customers use two different tool/function calling models: OpenAI-style 'tools' (name, description, json_schema) and our older 'functions' payloads (function_name, parameters, signature). This causes SDK fragmentation, duplicate handler code, and inconsistent streaming/error semantics. Goal: design a minimal adapter and migration path that: 1) allows the platform runtime and SDKs to accept OpenAI-style tools while preserving legacy function handlers; 2) provides clear naming resolution and telemetry; 3) documents streaming and structured-output behavior so client expectations are consistent.

Scope: runtime translation layer + SDK surface changes + migration docs. Not in scope: full deprecation of legacy functions in this cycle.

Non-goals: changing user-visible tool behaviours unless necessary for safety or correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime implements an adapter that accepts OpenAI-style 'tools' payload and emits equivalent legacy function invocation events for existing handlers.
Adapter preserves streaming tokens ordering and supports chunked structured-output fields without breaking existing streaming clients.
SDKs can opt-in to 'openai_tools' mode and receive tool metadata; default behavior remains backward compatible.
Migration guide published with example mappings, common pitfalls, and a test harness for customers to validate their handlers.
End-to-end tests added: 10+ scenarios covering name collisions, nested json_schema parameters, missing required params, and error propagation.
tasks: Design adapter interface and mapping rules (tech spec).
Implement runtime adapter in inference router (pooled service).
Add flag in SDKs to enable 'openai_tools' input mode and mapping utilities.
Create conversion tests and integrate into CI (unit + e2e streaming harness).
Draft migration doc and example notebooks for customers.
Run internal canary against beta users, collect telemetry, iterate.
decision_log: 2026-02-15: Chosen approach is a lightweight translation adapter (not a full rewrite) that normalizes OpenAI 'tools' into our internal function invocation schema before dispatch.
Key trade-offs: adapter preserves existing handler contracts to avoid breaking customers, but introduces a canonical 'tool_id' field to avoid relying on mutable 'name' strings.

Naming resolution: prefer explicit tool_id if provided by client; otherwise generate tool_id = slug(name) + '-' + stable-hash(signature). This balances human-readable names with uniqueness for routing and metrics.

Streaming model: keep server-side token streaming unchanged. For tool results emitted mid-stream, wrap structured outputs in a deterministic 'tool_response' event that clients can parse. This avoids interleaving partial structured fragments with free text tokens.

Error propagation: map runtime exceptions to a standard tool_failure object containing code, message, and optional raw_trace. Legacy handlers will receive the mapped structure under their existing failure channel.
Telemetry: tag all adapter-invoked calls with adapter_version and mapping_kind (openai->legacy or legacy->legacy) to track migration impact.

Backward compatibility toggle: implement 'compat_mode' to preserve old name-based routing for customers that cannot migrate immediately. 'compat_mode' defaults to true for one release cycle, then will warn.
comments: 2026-02-11 - Maya Patel: Initial write-up, uploaded tech spec stub to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/API/Tool-Adapter-Design. Please add feedback inline.

2026-02-16 - Diego Morales: Reviewed mapping rules. Concern: automatic slug+hash tool_id could break SSO-authored webhooks that expect names. Suggest adding an override header X-Tool-Id for advanced customers.

2026-02-18 - Luca Chen: Added prototype implementation in runtime branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/tool-adapter-prototype. Basic mapping works for top-level json_schema; need to handle oneOf/anyOf edge cases.

2026-02-25 - Priya Shah (PM): Request to include migration checklist and example for multi-tenant handlers that route by name. Also flag security implications for acceptance of arbitrary json_schema from customers.

2026-03-03 - Security review (notes): dynamic json_schema ingestion acceptable if schema size is limited to 64KB and we sanitize ref URIs. Link to notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Tool-Adapter-Security-Notes.

2026-03-08 - Design review: Decided to emit a stable 'tool_meta' block in the first stream event after invocation; SDKs can consume that to register a handler mapping before structured payloads begin.
2026-03-12 - QA: Added test failures for nested parameter coercion; created ISSUE temp ENG-5816 to follow up on coercion edge cases.

2026-03-12 - Luca Chen: Marking implementation as In Progress. Runtime PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1423. SDK changes draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/507.
risks: Name collisions where clients rely on human-readable 'name' for routing; mitigated by compat_mode and X-Tool-Id override.
Streaming incompatibilities for clients that parse free text tokens and expect tool outputs inline; mitigated by emitting 'tool_response' events and SDK helpers.
Schema injection / large schemas causing memory pressure; mitigated by schema size limits and sanitized refs as per security notes.
